common/src/main/java/org/keycloak/common/crypto/CryptoIntegration.java:57 - Removing the multiple-provider check lets the provider be chosen silently by classpath order when providers tie.. The old code failed fast when more than one `CryptoProvider` was on the classpath. Now the providers are sorted by `order()` and the first one wins. `DefaultCryptoProvider`, `WildFlyElytronProvider` and `FIPS1402Provider` all return 200, and the sort is stable, so when two of them are present the winner is whichever `ServiceLoader` finds first. The only trace is a debug log.

Trigger: a FIPS deployment that also has `keycloak-crypto-default` on its classpath by mistake used to refuse to start. Now it can quietly run with the non-FIPS BouncyCastle provider.

Fix: keep throwing when the top two providers have the same `order()`, so ties stay an error. Only the lower-priority authz-client provider should be skipped quietly.

common/src/main/java/org/keycloak/common/crypto/CryptoProvider.java:44 - Adding the abstract `order()` method to a public SPI breaks existing implementations.. `CryptoProvider` is a ServiceLoader SPI in `common`. Adding `int order()` with no body means any implementation that is not updated in this PR no longer compiles. That includes custom or third-party providers, and any test providers in other modules, which I could not check from here. An already-compiled implementation fails at runtime with `AbstractMethodError` when `detectProvider` sorts the list.

Fix: make it `default int order() { return 0; }` (or a similar baseline) and let the bundled providers override it.

authz/client/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/util/crypto/AuthzClientCryptoProvider.java:114 - Two encoder calls build values that are never used.. `ASN1Encoder.create().write(rBigInteger)` and `ASN1Encoder.create().write(sBigInteger)` build encoders and throw them away. The real encoding happens again inside `writeDerSeq` below. These two lines look like leftovers and should be removed.
